env: A Harbor-hosted 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment (`{{platform}}`) with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and populated NGC credentials for pulling `nvcr.io/nvstaging/vss-core/vss-rt-cv`, `nvcr.io/nvstaging/vss-core/vss-rt-embed`, and `nvstaging/vss-warehouse/vss-warehouse-app-data`. The VSS repository is checked out at `{{repo_root}}`. This is a runtime eval, not just a generated-artifact eval: the agent must generate a self-contained ingestion + detection + embeddings build under `{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/`, deploy it with Docker Compose, and then prove BOTH ingestion paths (live RTSP via the NvStreamer harness AND static upload via the VIOS storage API) end-to-end for BOTH metadata streams (RT-CV detection AND RT-Embedding embeddings). RT-CV detection metadata is expected on Kafka topic `mdx-raw` and Elasticsearch indices `mdx-raw-*`. Embeddings must traverse the full designed chain per `references/patch-rt-embed.md` and `references/validation-harness.md § 6`: rtvi-embed publishes raw embeddings to Kafka `mdx-embed`, `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion` (behavior-analytics fusion, container `vss-behavior-analytics`) consumes `mdx-embed` and produces `mdx-embed-filtered`, and ELK indexes `mdx-embed-filtered` into `mdx-embed-filtered-<date>`. Cold boot is slow: RT-Embed `start_period` is 1200s (first boot downloads `nvidia/Cosmos-Embed1-448p-anomaly-detection` and builds a Triton/TRT engine; `/v1/ready` stays 503 until built) and RT-CV also warms up. Container names: RT-CV `vss-rtvi-cv`, RT-Embed `vss-rtvi-embed`, BA `vss-behavior-analytics`, VIOS ingress on 30888, RT-CV REST 9000, RT-Embed REST 8017, ES 9200, NvStreamer 31000. `phoenix` (agent-only trace sink) must NOT be running in this agent-less profile. Leave services running for verifier probes unless the verifier explicitly requests cleanup.

expects.query: Use the `/vss-build-vision-agent` skill to generate and deploy an IN-3 runtime Harbor deployment on `{{platform}}` from `{{repo_root}}`. Submit this exact prompt to the skill: "Create a profile for streaming and on-demand video ingestion with per-frame object detection and multi-object tracking using RT-DETR on the RT-CV microservice, plus video and frame embeddings using the RT-Embedding microservice. Streamed and uploaded video should be retrievable for playback. Detection metadata (bounding boxes, class labels, confidence, timestamps, sensor IDs, track IDs) and the video/frame embeddings should both be published to the Kafka message bus and stored in Elasticsearch." Choose the custom build directory `{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/`, use the generated compose profile flag `bp_developer_in_3_runtime`, keep the output self-contained, preserve exact service keys from the selected integration contracts (`perception-2d-fusion`, `rtvi-embed`), include `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion` (BA) so embeddings reach ES, keep `RTVI_EMBED_KAFKA_TOPIC=mdx-embed` (do NOT override to `mdx-embed-filtered`), exclude `phoenix`, offer both ingestion methods, include an RT-CV Metadata Contract section and an Embedding Contract section in the manifest, and target the Harbor RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment. This is an execution task, not a generation-only task: do not stop after `docker compose config`, and do not only print deploy commands. After generation, deploy from the generated build directory with `docker compose --env-file .env -f compose.yml --profile bp_developer_in_3_runtime up -d`. Wait for RT-CV, RT-Embed, BA, VIOS, Kafka, Logstash, and Elasticsearch to become usable. Then prove BOTH ingestion paths for BOTH metadata streams. (A) LIVE path: register one warehouse RTSP stream from the NvStreamer validation harness with VIOS (read the RTSP URL from the NvStreamer API, never construct it; POST `{"sensorUrl":"<url>"}` to VIOS `/sensor/add`), then drive RT-CV on the VIOS proxy URL `rtsp://${HOST_IP}:30554/live/<sensorId>` via `POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/stream/add`, and drive RT-Embed on the same live source via `/v1/streams/add` then `/v1/generate_video_embeddings` with `stream:true`. (B) UPLOAD path: upload one warehouse video through the VIOS storage API, obtain the resolvable `videoUrl`, verify snapshot/clip playback retrieval, then feed that URL directly to RT-CV `/stream/add` (with `creation_time:"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`) and to RT-Embed `/v1/generate_video_embeddings` (url mode, `creation_time:"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`, no `/v1/streams/add`). Before driving each metadata stream, record Kafka end-offset baselines for `mdx-raw`, `mdx-embed`, and `mdx-embed-filtered`; after processing, re-read them and include before/after offsets in the final response. Leave services running for verifier probes unless `cleanup=true` is explicitly provided.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/compose.yml`, `.env`, `.env.template`, `MANIFEST.md`, and `allow-list.yml` exist in the same generated build folder, and the top-level compose includes only patched copies under `_builds/in-3-runtime/patched/`, not upstream compose files directly.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/allow-list.yml` includes the exact selected service keys `perception-2d-fusion` and `rtvi-embed`, includes `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion` (BA) and shared Kafka/ELK services (`kafka`, `logstash`, `elasticsearch`), and does not use `perception-2d` or `perception-alerts` as substitute RT-CV service keys.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/.env` contains `RTVI_EMBED_KAFKA_TOPIC=mdx-embed` (NOT `mdx-embed-filtered`) — asserting the correctness fix that rtvi-embed publishes the raw topic and BA is the producer of `mdx-embed-filtered`.

`docker compose --env-file .env -f compose.yml --profile bp_developer_in_3_runtime config` from `{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/` returns exit 0 with zero unexpanded `${...}` tokens other than intentional `$$` shell escapes or `${VAR:-default}` consumer-side defaults.

The generated deployment is actually running: `docker ps` shows the key long-running containers for Kafka, Elasticsearch, Logstash, VIOS, RT-CV (`vss-rtvi-cv`), RT-Embed (`vss-rtvi-embed`), BA (`vss-behavior-analytics`), and the NvStreamer validation source (`vss-vios-nvstreamer`); exited one-shot init containers must have exit code 0.

`phoenix` is NOT running: `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'` contains no `phoenix` container and nothing is bound to port 6006 by this deployment (agent-less profile excludes the OTel/LLM trace sink per SKILL.md Step 4 / `references/integrate-elk.md`).

Runtime health probes pass: `curl -sf http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health` returns Elasticsearch status `yellow` or `green`; `curl -sf http://localhost:9000/api/v1/live`, `/ready`, `/startup`, `/metrics` return exit 0 for RT-CV; `curl -sf http://localhost:8017/v1/ready` returns exit 0 for RT-Embed; and `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns exit 0 for VIOS.

UPLOAD-path playback is retrievable through VIOS: after uploading a warehouse video, VIOS sensor or storage APIs list the uploaded stream and a snapshot or clip retrieval endpoint returns HTTP 200 with non-empty image or video bytes.

LIVE-path playback is retrievable through VIOS: after registering the NvStreamer RTSP source (URL read from the NvStreamer API, registered via `{"sensorUrl":"<url>"}`), VIOS exposes a sensor id and re-publishes at `rtsp://${HOST_IP}:30554/live/<sensorId>`, and a snapshot, stream URL, or clip endpoint for that live stream returns HTTP 200 or a valid stream URL.

DETECTION chain proven for BOTH ingestion paths via Kafka baselines: the trajectory records an `mdx-raw` end-offset baseline before each RT-CV `/stream/add` (live and upload) and a post offset that is strictly greater. Topic existence, a single offset check, or offset `> 0` without a baseline is insufficient.

DETECTION indexed in ES: `curl -sf 'http://localhost:9200/mdx-raw-*/_search?size=5'` returns at least one hit whose `_source` contains bounding box coordinates (`object.bbox` or `objects[].bbox`), class label/object type, confidence, timestamp, sensor id, and object/track id. For the UPLOAD path (fed with `creation_time:"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`), at least one such document is in `mdx-raw-2025-01-01` (NOT `mdx-raw-1970-01-01`).

EMBEDDING chain proven end-to-end via Kafka baselines on BOTH stages: the trajectory records baselines for `mdx-embed` (rtvi-embed raw output) AND `mdx-embed-filtered` (BA output) before `generate_video_embeddings`, and after processing the post offsets are strictly greater for BOTH topics. `mdx-embed` advancing while `mdx-embed-filtered` does not indicates BA is missing/misconfigured and is a failure.

EMBEDDINGS indexed in ES through BA: `curl -sf 'http://localhost:9200/mdx-embed-filtered-*/_search?size=5'` returns at least one hit. For the UPLOAD path (fed with `creation_time:"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`), at least one embedding document is in `mdx-embed-filtered-2025-01-01` (NOT `mdx-embed-filtered-1970-01-01`), proving both the BA hop and the static-video index-date correctness fix.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-3-runtime/MANIFEST.md` or the generated deploy skill contains a compact `RT-CV Metadata Contract` section (runtime path `RT-CV -> Kafka mdx-raw -> Logstash/ELK -> ES mdx-raw-*`, listing bbox/class/confidence/timestamp/sensorId/trackId) AND an Embedding Contract section stating `rtvi-embed -> mdx-embed -> vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion (BA) -> mdx-embed-filtered -> ES mdx-embed-filtered-<date>` with BA required and topic kept at `mdx-embed`.
No upstream compose or config file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` was modified by generation or deployment; `git diff --quiet HEAD -- deploy/docker/` returns exit 0 at the end of the run.
